page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, which translates to a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated matrix operations. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (32.73 GB/sec) and text processing (2743.0 in Geekbench). General CPU benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (1926.0) and multi-core (7695.0), fall into the average performance tier.

The instance is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. While its DDR5 memory provides a high cached read bandwidth of 670.73 GB/sec for small blocks, uncached large-block read and write speeds are lower at 47.98 GB/sec and 44.81 GB/sec respectively. Passmark memory testing positions the memory subsystem in the lower performance tier (1800.86 score), highlighting a potential tradeoff for memory-bound workloads despite the high-speed DDR5 specification.

Given its compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 and dedicated CPU allocation, the c7i.2xlarge is structured for compute-heavy tasks. It is suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations, as evidenced by its 14.81 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 10.98 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It can also handle light machine learning inference, processing 135M parameter models at 154.29 tokens/sec for text generation, though performance drops significantly on larger 7B models.
